#Purpose: 
#Examining how wolf pup numbers are associated with moose abundance, wolf parasite load, and hunting permits.


#Data description:
#The ecological setting provides context for practising multiple regression; the data are not evidence about a real ecosystem. The predictor variables included in the dataset are the number of adult moose in the park (ADULTS), the number of moose calves born (CALVES), the average blood helminth load (WORMS) of trapped wolves (determined using blood samples from randomly selected wolves every year), and the number of moose hunting permits (PERMITS) issued by the park to human hunters.
#Source: Made up data for a practical excerise 

#Libraries ####
```{r}
library(car)
library(GGally)
library(performance)
library(tidyverse)
```

#Loaded the dataset
```{r}
df_WOLFPUPS<-read_csv("WOLFPUPS.csv")
```

#Data quality control ####
```{r}
str(df_WOLFPUPS)
plot(df_WOLFPUPS)

#Histograms for each predictor 
hist(df_WOLFPUPS$YEAR) #Datapoint from 2086??
hist(df_WOLFPUPS$ADULTS)
hist(df_WOLFPUPS$CALVES)
hist(df_WOLFPUPS$WORMS)
hist(df_WOLFPUPS$PERMITS)
hist(df_WOLFPUPS$PUPS)

df_WOLFPUPS.corr <- df_WOLFPUPS%>%
  filter(YEAR<2026)
```
#Removed the datapoint from 2086 as it was a mistake, then checking the corrected data
```{r}
plot(df_WOLFPUPS.corr)

hist(df_WOLFPUPS.corr$YEAR) 
hist(df_WOLFPUPS.corr$ADULTS)
hist(df_WOLFPUPS.corr$CALVES)
hist(df_WOLFPUPS.corr$WORMS)
hist(df_WOLFPUPS.corr$PERMITS)
hist(df_WOLFPUPS.corr$PUPS)
```

#Checking for colinearity
```{r}
ggpairs(df_WOLFPUPS.corr)
```

#Constructing a model and model diagnostics ####
```{r}
MOD.1<-lm(PUPS~ADULTS+
            CALVES+
            WORMS+
            PERMITS,
                  data=df_WOLFPUPS.corr)

check_model(MOD.1) #Adults and calves have high colinearity

MOD.2 <- update(MOD.1,~.- ADULTS)
check_model(MOD.2) #Colinearity is acceptable now

#Test if there is a difference in removing calves instead?
MOD.3 <- update(MOD.1,~.- CALVES)
check_model(MOD.3) #Not much of a difference 
```

#Model simplification ####
```{r}
summary(MOD.2) #Permits have the lowest effect
MOD.4 <- update(MOD.2,~.- PERMITS)
anova(MOD.2, MOD.4) #Test if new model is significantly worse 

summary(MOD.4)
#Test to try to remove the next one
MOD.5 <- update(MOD.4,~.- CALVES)
anova(MOD.4, MOD.5) #High F-value, so Calves should not be removed 

```

#Centering and scaling ####
```{r}
summary(MOD.4)
MOD.4s <- lm(PUPS ~ scale(CALVES) + scale(WORMS),
             data = df_WOLFPUPS.corr)
summary(MOD.4s) #Worms is the higher predictor

#Inspecting added variable plots
avPlots(MOD.4)
```

#Visualizing Partial Effects ####
```{r}
summary(df_WOLFPUPS.corr)
NEWPUPS_varWORMS <- crossing(WORMS = seq(0.01,1.22,
                                         length = 100),
                             CALVES = mean(df_WOLFPUPS.corr$CALVES),
                             PERMITS = mean(df_WOLFPUPS.corr$PERMITS))
NEWPUPS_varWORMS
NEWYUSINGWORMS <- predict(MOD.2,
                          newdata = NEWPUPS_varWORMS,
                          int = "c")
varWORMS_PREDS <- bind_cols(NEWPUPS_varWORMS,
                            as_tibble(NEWYUSINGWORMS))

```

#Plotting with ggplot ####
```{r}
ggplot(varWORMS_PREDS,
       aes(x = WORMS, y = fit)) +
  geom_line() +
  geom_point(data=df_WOLFPUPS.corr, #Adding points from the original dataset
             aes(x = WORMS, y= PUPS)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = lwr,
                  ymax = upr),
              alpha = 0.25) + # this argument makes the CI transparent
  labs(x = "WORMS",
       y = expression("PUPS")) +
  theme_bw()
```


#Result: ####

#The minimal adequate model of wolf recruitment rates showed a significant negative association with parasite load (Slope B =-6.77; Standardized regression coefficient Beta =-1.63; t =-3.68,P= 0.0007; see Figure 1A) and a positive association with the number of moose calves (B = 0.044, Beta = 1.26; t = 2.83; P = 0.0071; see Figure 1B). Because moose calf numbers were colinear with adult population size, we cannot distinguish between the effects of adults or calves on wolf recruitment

#Limitation: Wolf pup numbers may be affected by other predictors not studied as well.
